edits.walkthrough_append: Board takeaway: quote the result as 'the sum of any two sides of a triangle is greater than the third side', and in questions apply it to the two smaller sides only — that single check settles everything. Self-check: can 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm form a triangle? No — 3 + 4 = 7 is not greater than 8. Two-markers ask exactly this judgement; write the comparison line, not just yes or no.

Board takeaway: examiners watch the correspondence order — write the congruence statement only after matching corresponding parts, then read every equal side and angle straight off that order. Self-check: if triangle ABC corresponds to triangle RPQ, name the side equal to AB and the angle equal to angle C without drawing anything. Two marks hang on getting the order right the first time.

Board takeaway: when the given side is not between the given angles, say so plainly, compute the third angle by the angle sum, and then quote ASA with the side's new position. Self-check: two angles 50° and 60° with the side opposite the 50° angle — the third angle is 70°, and the given side now lies between the 60° and 70° angles, so ASA applies. That one reasoning line is what the method mark pays for.

Board takeaway: give two ultrasound applications, each with its reason — sonography because it images soft tissue without ionising radiation, flaw detection because even hairline cracks reflect the pulses back. Self-check: explain why the same waves are inaudible yet useful — a frequency beyond hearing does not stop reflection. A one-marker favourite asks why ultrasound is preferred over X-rays for fetal imaging; the expected phrase is 'no ionising radiation'.

Board takeaway: state the condition with the law — Ohm's Law holds at constant temperature — because numericals that heat a filament are testing exactly this caveat. Self-check: a 4 ohm resistor across 12 V carries 3 A; recompute the current if heating doubles the resistance. Papers set one straight substitution and one condition-based twist; be ready for both.

Board takeaway: always name the two bodies when applying the third law — the forces act on different objects, which is why they never cancel. Self-check: identify the action-reaction pair for a walker pushing the ground backwards, and for a gun recoiling after a shot. Recoil and swimming are the standard explain-why questions; the wording 'equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, acting on different bodies' must appear.

Board takeaway: quote the theorem as net work equals the change in kinetic energy, then substitute — the worked example above (49 − 9 = 40 J) is the exact format of a three-marker. Self-check: a 4 kg body slows from 6 m/s to 3 m/s; the work is ½ × 4 × (9 − 36) = −54 J, and the minus sign must be explained — the net work is done against the motion.

Board takeaway: a four-marker on Magadha's rise wants the three advantages named with one line each on how each helped — iron for superior weapons and tools, the Ganges for trade and taxable wealth, the fertile plain for surplus grain. Self-check: rank the three in your own order of importance and defend the ranking in one sentence; reasoned choice earns the evaluation mark.

Board takeaway: write the law in full — a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force — and attach one everyday proof, such as passengers lurching forward when a bus brakes. Self-check: explain that lurch using the inertia of the upper body, then answer why dust flies out of a beaten carpet. Both are standard two-markers on inertia.

Board takeaway: series numericals are marked on the chain — total resistance first, then the common current, then the individual voltage drops — so lay the steps out in exactly that order and close with the check that the drops add to the supply. Self-check: resistors of 1, 2 and 3 ohms across 6 V give 6 ohms and 1 A; state every drop before verifying their sum.

Board takeaway: write class intervals in exclusive (continuous) form unless told otherwise, and state the convention — the upper limit is excluded — because questions probe the 'which class holds 30?' ambiguity directly. Self-check: take the walkthrough's marks from 20 to 60, build the 20-30 and 30-40 classes, and show one borderline value (30) being entered in 30-40, not 20-30.

Board takeaway: relative-motion answers must name both frames — 'at rest relative to the train, in motion relative to the ground' — because half the marks sit in naming the frame. Self-check: a porter standing on a platform and a passenger on a passing train — state each one's state of motion in the other's frame. Expect one such statement question as a two-marker.

Board takeaway: organise a Chola answer around the three features — village assemblies, temple-centred administration, naval strength — with one concrete example each, such as the sabha inscriptions or the Srivijaya expedition. Self-check: explain in one line how temple treasuries and landholdings turned the temple into an administrative hub; that cause-effect sentence earns the explanation mark beyond bare facts.

Board takeaway: expect a two-part question — generate the first five terms from a recursive rule, then jump to a far term with an explicit rule — because the pair exposes the difference in efficiency. Self-check: for aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + 3 with a₁ = 4, list the terms (4, 7, 10, 13, 16) and then write the explicit rule aₙ = 4 + (n − 1) × 3 in one line.

Board takeaway: connect the fractal picture to the sequence in one line — stage n holds 3ⁿ small triangles — because the mathematics mark rides on the exponent, not the drawing. Self-check: how many small triangles appear at stage 5? 3⁵ = 243. Then say what happens to the total shaded area as the stages multiply; 'approaches zero' with the reason earns the extension mark.

Board takeaway: keep the arithmetic behind the 17-metre echo limit ready — distance equals speed × time ÷ 2, because sound travels to the surface and back. Papers regularly set the reverse problem: a cliff 85 m away gives an echo time of 0.5 s. Self-check: verify that example yourself, and write one line on why the division by 2 is needed.
